findings.description: The matching AssertionError label and nodeid do not bind actual internal failure cause or nested launcher rc. Unrelated nested failures can satisfy the accepted RED signature.

static_counterexamples.path: v5 precheck 491-504 appends a failed interpreter-probe reason to expected rewrite reasons; ok remains False; control 690 raises the same accepted prefix. Extra unrelated failure is not rejected.

v5 launch 735 disk_usage OSError caught at 770-771; meta write succeeds; returns 1 at 795 with prepare error, precheck None and postcheck None. Control 904 loads meta; 905 raises same accepted prefix. No launched child and no chained exception.
static_counterexamples.unchanged_expected_signature: AssertionError plus conditional-config prefix; ignored suffix can be None, None

static_counterexamples.path: v5 launch completes its normal child path but meta write 788 fails; catch 789-792 prints JSON and returns 4. Control 937 asserts rc==1 and raises exactly the same tuple as predicted rc==0, before meta read 938.

findings.outer_common_can_still_match: All nested failures are handled by the launcher; pytest finishes normally with the same 9 expected failed nodeids plus 24 passed and rc 1. External runner 525-543 checks its own cleanup, fixed-source hashes and records, not each test nested-launcher meta; these can remain normal, giving runner_ok=true and outer rc=1.
findings.minimum_correction: Add distinct UNEXPECTED-cause guards before the existing final assert in l23/l29/l30. For l23 accept pre.ok or only the exact intended rewrite reasons with successful source reads. For l29 accept rc0 or rc1 with normal precheck/child/cleanup/records and only the intended effective-URL postcheck mismatch. For l30 reject rc outside 0/1 and read/verify meta before the expected RED assert, requiring rc0 to be a normal complete launch. Existing named tests and expected final asserts can remain, preserving 33 tests, 9+24 RED and 71 GREEN. Rebind modified control hashes and step-runner seals.

finding_not_claimed: No deterministic mismatch of the nine expected first-failure locations was found from code reading; 9+24 is still only a static prediction. The finding concerns false acceptance of other handled failures, not ordinary pytest formatting.
